notes: Gotvald, Barth, Veilleux and Parrett, SIR 2012-5113 (no revisions listed): six hydrologic regions (plate 1) at 8 AEPs (50-0.2 percent). Equations from Table 5 (p. 14); AVP and SEP from Table 6 (p. 16); model error variance and covariance matrix U from Table 8 (pp. 18-19), order intercept then the variables as printed (Sierra Nevada: DRNAREA, ELEV, PRECIP); ranges from Table 9 (p. 20). Storage: intercept = log10 of the printed coefficient; every variable log10 (the report's power form), including Sierra Nevada's ELEV with its negative exponent. Variable codes are NSS's: DRNAREA (GIS drainage area, mi2), PRECIP (mean annual precipitation, in.), ELEV (mean basin elevation, ft). sep_log is Table 6's SEP percent converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10), which equals sqrt(AVP) under the report's eq. 6; avp is Table 6's AVP; model_error_variance is Table 8's sigma_delta^2. n_sites per region is the number of Table 2 streamgages in the region less those footnoted r (not used: redundant) and n or p (frequency undetermined): 184, 54, 199, 95 and 98 for regions 1-5, 630 in all as the report states (p. 14), and 33 for the desert region. With p = 3 or 4 parameters these reproduce the report's printed t(0.05, n-p) of 1.653, 1.675, 1.653, 1.662 and 1.661 (eq. 9). The desert region (6) has no regression: its equations come from regional LP3 parameters (a constant standard deviation of 0.91 log units, a mean linear in log drainage area, zero skew; appendix), so Table 8 gives no model error variance or covariance and intervals use sep_log; its SEP runs from 214 to 856 percent. Checks: Table 5 was entered from the rendered page and every equation equals the NSS snapshot (2026-10-25) coefficient for coefficient, with the same ranges; Table 6 agrees between the rendered page and pdftotext; every Table 8 matrix is symmetric, and model_error_variance + x'Ux reproduces Table 10's regression variance of prediction (column R) at 732 of the 734 regression-region gages within 0.0006 at every AEP (median 0.0001-0.0005, Table 8's 3-decimal rounding of sigma_delta^2). The two exceptions are Table 10 itself at one or two AEPs: 11099500 (Sawpit Creek) at 0.2 percent, and 11247200 (Big Sandy Creek tributary) at 0.5 and 0.2 percent, whose other AEPs agree. Worked examples (p. 25): North Coast Q1% at DRNAREA 27.8, PRECIP 32.7 = 6,000 ft3/s (6,003 computed) and at DRNAREA 25.0, PRECIP 32.5 = 5,460 ft3/s (5,457). Out of scope: NSS's four Thomas and others (1997, WSP 2433) regions it also lists for California (GC29, GC30, GC31, GC307), superseded here; the urban adjustment (Tables 11-12) and the weighting procedures are not equations of this kind.
